name: Migrations Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday migrations work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical migrations tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday migrations work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical migrations tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When migrations decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen migrations approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Check that migrations terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Measure before optimizing any migrations bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. State assumptions about migrations explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Before starting migrations work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Prefer the simplest migrations approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated migrations concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new migrations abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic migrations advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of migrations correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these migrations guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
